notes: Primary contact: Head of Product (Maya Singh) — wants agent to autonomously run search + create/update tickets in their system.
Use-case detail: chat assistant that can look up account docs, call internal actions (create support ticket, escalate), and return a concise summary to user.
Constraint: strict latency expectation for interactive UX. P95 streaming target ~200-250ms. If tool-call adds >500ms the UX degrades.

Concerns voiced repeatedly: tool-call reliability (timeouts vs retries) — "If the agent times out on a tool call we get inconsistent state and bad UX", wants idempotency and strong retry/fallback behaviors.
Customer asked about Redwood features: streaming + function calling, customizable retry policies, automatic fallback to cheaper model variants on overload, prefix caching for repeated queries.

POC success metrics (customer-specified): 1) P95 token latency for streaming under 250ms at 50 concurrent sessions; 2) tool-call success rate > 99% under baseline load; 3) cost per session within target range in pricing deck.

SE notes: will instrument end-to-end traces and surface token-level cost/latency in Redwood Console; propose canary with model fallback and shorter timeout window for tool calls + compensating retries.
Pricing note: Riverbend leans toward Hosted for low friction POC; if Dedicated clearly reduces unit cost and meets latency SLO they will contract Dedicated for production (12mo commit likely).
Action items: Redwood to deliver POC test harness, sample canary rollout config, and a short runbook for handling tool-call timeouts (fallback strategies + reconcilers).
Quote from product lead: "We need predictable UX — streaming must feel instantaneous and tool calls must not create silent failures."
